purpose: Upgrade strong compact canonical relations identified by the manifest quality report with sequence, counterpressure, supported conclusion, reusable scenes and reader-facing significance.

project_sequence: one guardian placed to the right
one guardian placed to the left
a narrow gate to Heaven placed between them
later same-day material distinguishes a cube surrounding Heaven
biblical_sequence: cherubim guard the way to the Tree of Life
Matthew's teaching urges entry through the narrow gate
John's discourse identifies Jesus as the Door through which sheep enter, exit and find pasture
relation_argument.why_dense: The project-side image already contains guardians, a narrow central passage, Jesus at the passage and a higher divine destination; the biblical comparison is therefore a bundle of access-control functions rather than a one-word gate match.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It shows that Door theology is most useful when read as a system of access, guardianship, passage and destination—not merely as a title applied to the Son.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: A dense later comparison to biblical guarded-way, narrow-gate and Door traditions is defensible. The biblical texts do not depict two modern guardians flanking Jesus, do not place Eden's gate at the North Pole and do not supply the project's surrounding cube.

enrichments.mismatch: Genesis places cherubim east of Eden guarding the way to the Tree of Life; Matthew's narrow gate and John's Door belong to separate teachings. The modern scene combines these distinct texts into one architecture, and its cube/North arrangement is project-specific.

project_sequence: public/project formulation invokes Lion of Judah
Root of David is joined to the same formulation
Potato of Life, Father and Son roles are clustered around those titles
biblical_sequence: Genesis gives Judah lion and ruler imagery
Revelation announces the Lion of Judah and Root of David
John then sees a slain-yet-standing Lamb who is able to open the scroll
correspondences: Revelation joins victory to a wounded Lamb rather than simple domination
relation_argument.why_dense: Several distinct Davidic and Revelation title families are joined in one dated project formulation, while Revelation itself complicates Lion language by revealing the victorious figure as a slain-standing Lamb.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The comparison is strongest as a test of how kingship is understood: the biblical Lion/Root complex redirects triumphal power toward wounded, sacrificial and revelatory power.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The project explicitly appropriates recognizable biblical royal/messianic titles. This supports a strong documented self-mapping at the level of language and symbolism, not proof that modern Father/Son roles are identical with Revelation's Christological figure.

enrichments.mismatch: Genesis, Isaiah and Revelation have their own Judah/David/Christological contexts. Revelation's Lion and Lamb are one visionary figure, whereas the project can distribute Lion, Root, Father and Son functions differently.

project_sequence: recovered Tim vocabulary invokes a chariot of light
the chariot is explicitly brought into relation with Ezekiel/wheels imagery
later comparative work places the image inside the project's wheel/Axis/Spirit field
biblical_sequence: Ezekiel sees storm, fire and living creatures
an expanse and throne-like structure appear above
the vision culminates in the likeness of divine glory and Ezekiel falls
relation_argument.why_dense: The project explicitly names Ezekiel/wheels rather than researchers supplying the association from a generic circle or spiral. The whole vision also contributes movement, Spirit and throne relations beyond the isolated wheel image.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Reading the complete scene prevents 'Ezekiel's wheel' from becoming a free-floating geometry claim: the wheels function inside a mobile divine-throne vision whose center is coordinated movement and presence.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The dated project vocabulary deliberately invokes Ezekiel's wheel/chariot imagery. It does not establish that Ezekiel described a potato, a modern vehicle, Saturn, or the project's exact geometry.

enrichments.mismatch: Ezekiel's wheels belong to a complex prophetic throne vision with living creatures, Spirit, expanse and divine glory. The text gives no exact Potatoverse geometry and should not be reduced to a literal modern object.

project_sequence: thought-archive formulation identifies the Son as Messiah
the Son is also identified as Door
New Jerusalem, North throne and Father are placed in the same relational cluster
biblical_sequence: John 10 identifies Jesus as the Door and then Good Shepherd
Revelation later presents New Jerusalem descending from God
the city becomes divine-human dwelling with gates, river and Tree of Life
relation_argument.why_dense: The project does not merely borrow one title: it joins person, access function, sacred city, throne/source and dwelling imagery in one relational cluster.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: The comparison clarifies a useful distinction inside the project: the Son can function as access/threshold while New Jerusalem functions as destination/dwelling; collapsing Door and City into one object would lose the biblical role structure.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Explicit biblical/Christian vocabulary is present on the project side. John and Revelation provide strong comparative functions, but they do not identify New Jerusalem with the North Pole, Tim, or a modern geopolitical throne.

enrichments.mismatch: John's Door discourse and Revelation's New Jerusalem vision are separate texts and objects. Revelation's city descends from heaven and does not locate itself at the geographic North Pole.
